title: Node leak while using `scene_painted` signal
body:
### Tested versions

Master

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev (5e0fa394d) - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor (1600x900 @ 60.00 Hz) - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated Radeon RX 560 Series (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 31.0.21912.14) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-4570 CPU @ 3.20GHz (4 threads) - 15.93 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

I noticed that when using the new `scene_painted` (#122981) signal from `ScenePaint2DEditor`, we can create dynamic brushes that procedurally generate content or locations, for example, by creating a flower, we can generate several more random flowers nearby, but the created nodes are not displayed in the `SceneTree`, and they cannot be selected or deleted.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c85d0bcc-fa3f-438a-912c-bfcd74ea53fb

It's likely that this kind of freedom of action could lead to SceneTree breaking. I'm considering replacing the signal with #122859, or should we just warn the user about this in the documentation?



### Steps to reproduce

Set this script on the node you are going to draw with:
```
@tool
extends Node2D

var _paint_editor: ScenePaint2DEditor

func _enter_tree() -> void:
	_paint_editor = EditorInterface.get_scene_paint_2d()
	_paint_editor.connect("scene_painted", _on_scene_painted)

func _exit_tree() -> void:
	if _paint_editor and _paint_editor.is_connected("scene_painted", _on_scene_painted):
		_paint_editor.disconnect("scene_painted", _on_scene_painted)

func _on_scene_painted(node: Node2D) -> void:
	var r = preload("res://node_2d.tscn").instantiate() as Node2D
	add_child(r)
	r.position = node.position + Vector2(randf_range(-100,100),randf_range(-100,100))
```
